instruction: Capture the present video frame and store it on the Desktop using the filename 'screenshotYYYYMMDD.png', with YYYYMMDD representing today's date.

parameters.window_name: Interstellar Movie - Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer - VLC media player

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires capturing a video frame and saving with a timestamped filename (e.g., screenshot_20231215.png or screenshot20231215.png). The evaluator uses wildcard pattern to find the file and checks: (1) file exists on Desktop, (2) filename contains timestamp pattern (YYYYMMDD, HHMMSS, or similar date/time format), (3) file is valid PNG. This tests ability to generate dynamic filenames with date/time information.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses strict regex '^screenshot[_-]?(\d{8})\.png$' to match exactly YYYYMMDD format (8 consecutive digits), rejecting other timestamp formats
Getter properly extracts date value from filename and validates it (year 1900-2100, month 1-12, day 1-31)
Metric correctly compares extracted date_value with today's date using datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d'), ensuring the date is actually today
Getter validates PNG format by actually opening file with PIL Image.verify(), not just checking extension
All instruction requirements are verified: file exists on Desktop, filename has YYYYMMDD format, date is today, file is valid PNG
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The regex allows optional separator [_-]? which accepts 'screenshot20251222.png', 'screenshot_20251222.png', or 'screenshot-20251222.png'. Instruction says 'plus' which could imply direct concatenation only, but current implementation is more user-friendly and still correct.
